title: opt aborts at startup: near no-wrap recovery pass and its switch share one option name
summary: MOSRecoverNearNoWrap registered its legacy pass argument and its -mos-recover-near-nowrap cl::opt under the same string. opt turns every registered legacy pass into a command-line option, so any opt containing the MOS target aborted at startup before reading input; llc and clang were unaffected. The pass is now named mos-near-nowrap-recovery and inserted by ID, in 0002 and in the upstream extraction; the switch keeps its name. The preserved downstream opt aborts on verify.ll and the rebuilt one exits 0; the downstream MOS suites now pass 186 with 3 unsupported and no failures.
attribution: Structured record, preserved baseline and extraction repair: Claude Code 2.1.283, model Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), xhigh reasoning effort; session f79adc39-72b4-4dc5-abc1-849c14c5ce96.
Earlier sightings are credited in docs/investigations/2026-09-28-farblit-range-integration.md and docs/defects/mos-xy16-stale-x-writer-reload.json.
Downstream repair and closure: Claude Code 2.1.283, model Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), xhigh reasoning effort; session f79adc39-72b4-4dc5-abc1-849c14c5ce96.
unknowns: The exact vendor dirty state linked into the preserved downstream baseline opt was not captured; its diagnostic names the colliding string.

prior_work.source_assessment: vendor/llvm-mos/llvm/lib/Target/MOS/MOSRecoverNearNoWrap.cpp uses "mos-recover-near-nowrap" for both the cl::opt and INITIALIZE_PASS_BEGIN/END. Destination 06bc967d2668 has no such pass.
prior_work.binary_assessment: build/llvm-mos/bin/opt (built 2026-09-28) is preserved by hard link as build/near-nowrap-option-clash/baseline/opt and reproduces the abort. The extracted revision 98984efd reproduces it; the final extraction 43e1c4d6 does not.
prior_work.decision: Distinct from mos-near-index-overflow-proofs: that record tracks the missed indexed-addressing optimization, while this one is a pass-registration defect in the same file that aborts opt before any code generation. llc and clang do not build the legacy pass-name option parser, so the optimization evidence is unaffected. Two September 28 audits recorded this collision only as a qualification of suite results; this is its first structured record.

configuration.expected: opt starts and verifies the module

additional_runs.result: The same verify.ll command exits 134 with the duplicate-registration signature on the first extraction and 0 on the final extraction, whose pass argument is mos-near-nowrap-recovery. MOS CodeGen+MC suites: first extraction 139 passed, 5 failed (the five opt-based tests), 1 unsupported; repaired extraction 144 passed, 1 unsupported. The extracted regression adds an opt startup RUN line.

resolution.change: patches/llvm-mos/0002-321-accum16.patch (pass argument DEBUG_TYPE mos-near-nowrap-recovery, ID-based insertion after LSR, MOSRecoverNearNoWrap.h) and patch 2 of docs/pr-preparations/2026-09-29/near-index-proofs
resolution.causal_explanation: PassNameParser registers every legacy pass argument as an opt option. INITIALIZE_PASS used "mos-recover-near-nowrap", the same name as the cl::opt switch, so opt reported a duplicate registration and aborted during target initialization. Distinct names remove the duplicate; llc and clang never instantiate the parser, which is why they were unaffected.
resolution.trigger_check: The same opt -passes=verify command on the retained verify.ll exits 134 with the duplicate-registration signature on the preserved baseline and 0 on the rebuilt downstream opt. near-index-proofs.ll carries an opt startup RUN line, and the five opt-based MOS lit tests pass again.

configuration.expected: opt starts and verifies the module

candidate.toolchain_location: build/near-nowrap-option-clash/candidate/opt (hard link of build/llvm-mos/bin/opt rebuilt 2026-09-29 from vendor with the updated 0002)
